questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a hard time finding study destinations, where I could get the modules I needed. Limerick ended up being one of the only options I found, and I thought it was a plus, that I would receive an Erasmus grant and that Ireland is rich in beautiful nature and interesting culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really had a great time and met the best people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Limerick sent out emails with a lot of information prior to arrival. They were really helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation week for exchange and erasmus students, that supplied us with a lot of helpful information, and social events to help you meet new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really difficult to find housing! I sadly did not get accommodation on campus, and I took me quite a while to find housing off campus. University of Limerick has an off campus coordinator, who was really helpful, and was the one who eventually found an apartment for me. Do not hesitate to ask for help from the coordinator!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In most cases, it will end up being really expensive. I had to pay 1000 euros a month in rent, not including electricity. The quality of the housing is generally very bad. My apartment was pretty cold and a bit mouldy, as it was badly isolated. However, it is important not to be too picky - remember that you are only there for 4 months.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember exact process, but we just had to give them relevant information, make a preliminary list of 10 modules, apply for accommodation, etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: University of Limerick was really helpful, as they supplied step-by-step instructions on how to registrer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The final registration for classes is done in the second-third week of the semester - I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I found University of Limerick to be very helpful - it was more the other processes, such as the learning agreement, that I found complicated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the content of the modules to be easier, than at KU. However, the workload was higher, as we had more assignments, exams and midterms. The second part of the semester had a pretty heavy workload, while the first part was very easy to get through, and felt a lot easier than what I was used to at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier than at KU in terms of the theories and the content we had to learn - but I found the workload pretty intense in the latter part of the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not as much student engagement in the modules I had - most of it was just lectures. The style of teaching at KU is focused on being able to use different theories and think critically - this I found to be a lot less prominent in the teachings at University of Limerick. Much of the content of the modules were taught as factual or "this is the way it is", which I found to be a bit simplistic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced research methods, The Psychology of Work, Principles of Human Resource Management, Developmental Psychopathology and Sociology of Race and Racisms.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of Race and Racisms! Very, very interesting module. Gave really good insight into both historic and contemporary issues - and also gave insight in Irelands history.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Electricity was not included in my rent - and electricity is super expensive in Ireland!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive - but the cost of living I would say was less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UL has a whole bunch of clubs and societies, so everyone can find something they enjoy.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stables, the on-campus bar, hosted international night every friday. There were so many different clubs and societies available - I tried yoga, outdoor pursuits club, dance and archery.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the yoga society and Outdoor Pursuits Club - OPC organised hikes every weekend, and also a few weekend trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! I went on trips to Galway, Cork, Belfast and Derry. Getting around to the different cities were fairly easy. There is also a few companies that organises daytrips on the weekends to different locations in Ireland. Through them I went to Dingle, to Aran Islands and Cliffs of Moher. Many of these places can be quite difficult to reach unless you have access to a car - so if not, I would recommend going on some of these trips. I also did some hiking trips with my friends - we went to Moylussa, which was a really nice mountain, not too far by bus from Limerick.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy. Irish people are really nice, and the orientation week made people settle in pretty quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and societies, that would be your best opportunity to meet Irish people. But they are generally more talkative and outgoing than danish people, so you would also often socialise with locals, when you went out to different pubs. However, the Irish students are often a lot younger, than what I was used to from Denmark. They could be as young as 17 years old, and I sometimes found the age different to be pretty apparent. I spent my time with other exchange students, which I did not regret. The other exchange students were closer in age, and I really enjoyed that we were having the same experience - everyone is really open, and everyone wants to make the most of their time on exchange.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The nightlife is quite different - people go out quite early and they really dress up, in miniskirts etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how friendly the Irish people are. I also love the nature, and the pub culture with live traditional music.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Limerick is probably not going to be your favourite city. Coming from Copenhagen, it was a very different experience to stay in Limerick, as it is not the most beautiful city and not a lot of stuff is going on. However, I would just embrace it. You are only there for a short while - and I would say that it made my experience better in some ways. It is part of the experience to try something different, and it was a lot of fun, to build a life for yourself in a place, where you maybe couldn't picture yourself beforehand. 

Another thing is, just be open and say yes to things. An exchange semester passes by so quickly, so just try to be present and enjoy it. Don't get to stressed out about academic matters - it will probably work out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really met some amazing people, that I built very close friendships with. We had a lot of fun. It was also very rewarding to have a semester away from my busy life at home. At home I have more obligations - uni, work, different friend groups, volunteering, family, etc. It was really nice to have a semester where I only had to focus on two things - my exchange friends and my schoolwork. I loved the spontaneity that followed from this, and having a friendgroup that I hung out with almost everyday - both at university and outside of it. An exchange semester is still very busy, but just in different ways. There is also going to be things you won't find the time to do, because you want to do it all, while you are there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saying goodbye to my friends when I had to go home. It is hard to say goodbye to people when you have been used to seeing them everyday, and then not knowing if and when you are going to see them again, when you all go home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go!! It is going to be such a nice experience!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
